Several evaluations are partially circular. Conditional fidelity is measured using the same geometric moments optimized by the guidance loss, and the morphological metrics are also based on closely related moment features, so improved scores do not strongly demonstrate anatomical realism or simulation readiness.

The baseline comparison is not fully convincing. The conditional dropout baseline is disadvantaged for cases with few or no constraints, and the fully constrained setting appears much closer; the paper does not isolate whether gains come from the proposed guidance or from baseline design choices and tuning.

Reproducibility is incomplete: manual filtering criteria, random seeds, code/model availability, and statistical uncertainty are not sufficiently specified for a high-stakes medical generative modeling paper.

The paper lacks a substantive ethics and safety discussion despite using medical data and proposing synthetic anatomy for clinical research and device evaluation workflows. Risks from anatomically invalid generations, privacy, and misuse are not adequately addressed.
